sentences.text: The revision being arguable is admitted for hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No.18119/2023, which is first application filed under Section 397(1) of Cr.P.C. on behalf of applicant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

The applicant has been convicted by the appellate Court under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for six months and fine of Rs.1,000/-,
with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the trial Court has n o t properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record.
Maximum sentence awarded to the applicant is six months R.I.

The final disposal of this revision will take considerable time, therefore,
the jail sentence of the applicant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, perused the records and the judgments of the Courts below.
In this application for suspension of sentence it has been argued that applicant is 100 percent disabled and he was not present when the samples of food items were taken.
The facts of the case reveal that applicant was the manufacturer and supplier of those food items to District Hospital Dindori working under the establishment of Jain Bhojanalaya.

Admittedly, applicant was not present when the samples were taken and his employee, who was serving the food had also fled away, but no case is made out to suggest that there was any tampering in the contents of the food items and the samples thereof.

Merely for the reason of non-presence of applicant at the time of taking samples or that the applicant is suffering from any physical disability, no case about innocence of applicant or showing leniency in his favour is made out.
